newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai minister says 1996 GDP may fall below target.
newsitem.headline: Thai minister says 1996 GDP may fall below target.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said that slow exports this year could pull the country's gross domestic product (GDP) growth below the government's target of 7.8 percent.

Bodi told reporters late on Sunday night he was still optimistic that the GDP growth would at least reach seven percent in 1996, but said there was a possibility the growth rate could slide below seven percent.

"If the export figures for June and July that we received were correct, it is possible that the GDP growth this year would be as Olarn forecast," he said, referring to the forecast by Thai Banker Association President Olarn Chaiprawat that 1996 GDP growth would be at 6.8 percent.
Thailand posted average economic growth of 9.8 percent since 1987, according to a recent report by Peregrine. In 1995, the growth rate was 8.6 percent.
Bodi said export-boosting tax measures introduced earlier this month were expected to yield tangible results in the next two to three months.
"For the year 1996, the impact of the measures could be felt by the end of the year. But the more obvious results would be seen in 1997," he said.

In a move to boost lagging exports, Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's administration announced a wide-ranging tax and savings incentive package under which Thailand will cut or lift tariffs on several dozen imported materials in various sectors.
Exports grew only 3.8 percent in the first six months of 1996, against a 26.2 percent rise in the same period last year, Bank of Thailand figures show.
Analysts have been lowering their projections for Thailand's economic growth to between 6.2 percent and 7.3 percent.
Bodi defended Thailand's economic performance, saying the fall in export growth was a regional trend and not unique to Thailand.
He said that among Thailand's exports, the troubled sectors like textiles, shoes, and frozen shrimp account for only 22 percent of export revenue.
Thirteen other items belong to bullish sectors such as computer components and electronic products, he said. They accounted for 43 percent of export revenue.
"These products still have a bright future... We believe that the economy should head toward a better direction by the end of the year," he said.
